id_and_class.theory_title: Brand Deisler’s Linguistically Attributed Biographical Self and Conscious Action
id_and_class.summary: Guillermo Brand Deisler proposes that the human Self is built developmentally from other people’s talk about a child: statements such as ‘Peter fell’ or ‘Peter will visit the park tomorrow’ construct a biography around the child’s name, which becomes coupled to the organism’s own accumulated history. Once stable, this biographical entity becomes the referent to which the brain unconsciously attributes actions, and an action is ‘conscious’ in his technical sense when it is attributed to the Self in this way. The theory takes basic sentience as given and explains how experience becomes organized around a persisting person.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: The Self as a Biography Built From Others’ Words

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Brand Deisler identifies the human Self with a biographical entity constructed through linguistic attribution and conscious action with action that unconscious functioning attributes to that entity; he does not identify phenomenal consciousness itself with anything.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: All processes sustaining action occur in the organism, while actions are individuated at the biographical level. He calls the Self a ‘living entity’ without a body of its own, yet it depends entirely on the organism’s material organization and has no causal power outside it.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Basic sentience is presupposed rather than explained; the biographical Self emerges developmentally from language and memory (weak emergence).
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Feeling can come before the Self: an infant or animal may feel pain without a temporally extended biographical self. The Self later adds autobiographical ‘mineness’, the sense that an action is mine, and the difference between something happening in me and something I am doing.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: The theory explicitly excludes qualia and does not explain why red looks red or pain hurts. It holds that attribution to the Self can change a feeling’s salience, emotional tone, and personal meaning without creating its quality.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A sentient organism, its ‘operative present’ (an updated functional organization of bodily and environmental information), its Functional Autobiography of acquired modifications, and biographies linked to persisting referents.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Through developmental observation of how children acquire self-reference and through findings on memory, language, attribution, attention, and action.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: Two organizations coupled without fusion: the organism’s Functional Autobiography, which perceives, feels, and acts bodily, and the language-built biography of the named person, which organizes the person’s past, present, and possible future actions.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Selfhood, agency, conscious action (in a technical sense), autobiographical memory, planning, and reflective self-awareness; not elementary phenomenal experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Coincident attributions (‘Peter is running’ while the child runs) couple the name-centered biography to the organism, while non-coincident attributions (‘Peter broke the glass yesterday’) make the referent independent of present activity.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Over development, speakers no longer need to supply attributions; present situations activate the biographical referent automatically, and the Self emerges when it works stably as the target of unconscious action attribution.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Realized within the organism’s brain, though the biography’s content concerns past, future, and possible worlds the body does not occupy.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: The Self lets the organism act in relation to times and worlds beyond the present, through remembering, planning, promising, and reconsidering, and it affects which contents reach the foreground of attention.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Attributing experiences to one persisting Self links episodes separated in time and places sensations, emotions, and thoughts within a single personal trajectory.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: Language expands the operative present so absent, past, future, fictional, and abstract entities can take part in cognition, just as a child tracks Little Red Riding Hood across a story.
core_claims_and_evidence: The human Self is neither innate nor presupposed but is built from other people’s third-person statements about the child.
The attribution that makes an action the Self’s own is unconscious and need not take the form of inner speech.
Remembering, in his restricted sense, is integrating earlier content into the present as belonging to the Self’s biographical past.
Information about one’s own name, reputation, commitments, or future gains unusual relevance and so shapes attention and experience.
mechanism_and_dynamics.basis_of_belief_or_evidence_type: Theoretical synthesis of developmental, linguistic, and cognitive findings; the full developmental sequence is hypothetical.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: Calling the Self a ‘living entity’ rests on a broad operational definition of life and is philosophically contestable. Using ‘conscious action’ for action attributed to the Self departs from the usual sense of the term, since such actions need not be experienced.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: The theory does not explain why any process is accompanied by experience or why agency feels like anything, and its developmental sequence still needs empirical confirmation.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent within naturalism, since the Self depends wholly on material organization. It shares themes with Mead, Vygotsky, Dennett, and Damasio while proposing its own mechanism.

AI_consciousness.rationale: The theory presupposes a sentient organism and does not say whether a machine could have that sentience, though a language-built Self could in principle be attributed to one.

survival_beyond_death.rationale: Since the Self depends entirely on organization realized in the organism and has no causal power outside it, nothing of it survives the organism’s death.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Personal meaning comes from the socially constructed biography of a person, with no cosmic purpose.

virtual_immortality.rationale: A biography could be recorded or modeled, but the theory ties the Self to a living organism’s Functional Autobiography and does not address transfer.
